candidate_sentence_map.S1: AB Amber Grid reported a significant improvement in financial performance for the three-month period ended 31 March 2026.

candidate_sentence_map.S16: The company continues to manage a legal dispute regarding guarantee funds for the GIPL pipeline, with a provision of EUR 5,815 thousand recognized for potential repayment.
candidate_sentence_map.S17: In April 2026, the General Meeting of Shareholders approved a dividend distribution of EUR 9,989 thousand.

details.completeness_justification: All seven key information units are fully represented in the candidate summary. K1 is covered by revenue growth and volume/price drivers (S2, S3). K2 is covered by the reported EBITDA and net-profit surges (S7, S9). K3 is covered by the explicit adjusted-EBITDA figure (S11). K4 is covered by the natural-gas-cost reduction and the Kaliningrad-transit explanation (S5, S6). K5 is covered by the net-debt increase and the covenant-related reclassification (S13, S14). K6 is covered by the Alvora litigation and provision (S16). K7 is covered by the post-period dividend approval (S17). No material omissions remain.
details.coherence_justification: The candidate summary is internally coherent. Each sentence follows logically from the preceding ones: revenue growth (S2) is explained by volume and price changes (S3) and offset by a decline in balancing revenue (S4); the resulting cost reduction (S5–S6) directly supports the EBITDA and EBIT increases (S7–S8) and the net-profit and EPS figures (S9–S10). The adjusted-EBITDA figure (S11) is presented as a distinct regulatory adjustment without contradicting the unadjusted results. Balance-sheet movements (S12–S15) are presented chronologically and causally linked to the reclassification events described in S14. The legal provision (S16) and dividend approval (S17) are standalone statements that do not conflict with any prior data. No self-contradictions, logical gaps, organizational disorder, or unnecessary repetition are present.
